events.name: The Rival's Missing Ace

success.text:
You crouch down and start putting their things back in the bag. They let you. That alone says a lot.

**{rival}:** "It was my first. Before I was any good."

They walk beside you after that, close, scanning every bush. The road ahead bends toward the trees.

You mean it kindly. It lands like a door closing.

**{rival}:** "Sure. It'll come back." They say it flat, the way you say a thing you've decided not to believe.

They gather the bag, and go alone. You hear them calling a name, down the road, until you can't.

They look at you for a long moment. They don't argue. That is worse.

**{rival}:** "Right. Of course."

They pick up the bag, and walk the other way. Later, much later, you hear them finding it alone.

events.name: The Rival's Missing Ace: The Second Step
events.intro:
You search the roadside together: the ditch, the hollow log, the mouth of a drainage pipe. {rival} calls its name, over and over, less loudly each time.

**{rival}:** "I shouted at it. After the loss. I've never done that."

They don't look at you when they say it. They look at the ground, where a small set of tracks leads off the road.

success.text: The tracks are small and careful, a Pokémon that didn't want to be followed and didn't quite try to hide. You go on, together.

events.name: The Rival's Missing Ace: The Third Step
events.intro:
The tracks cross a stream and climb a bank. {rival} stops at the top, hands on their knees. They're not out of breath.

**{rival}:** "If it's gone, I don't think I do this any more."

You have never heard them say anything that large. A long way off, on the wind, you hear a sound: something striking something, again and again.

success.text: You push through the last of the brush. The sound gets louder, and then it gets very steady.

events.name: The Rival's Missing Ace: The Clearing
events.intro:
A clearing. The ace is there, alone, in the middle of it, practising the move that failed. Over and over. The same motion, the same stumble, the same start again.

It hasn't eaten. It hasn't rested. It hasn't noticed you. {rival} has stopped breathing, a little, beside you.

success.text:
**{rival}:** "I'm sorry. It wasn't you. It was me."

The ace turns. It looks at {rival} for a long time, then walks over, and stands against their leg like it never left. They don't say anything else, and neither do you.

effects.text: Helped the rival find the ace that walked away, and stayed to see it come home.

success.text:
You step back through the brush, until the clearing is only light between leaves. Someone is speaking, low, a long way off. You don't hear what's said.

You wait on the bank until {rival} comes up the path, eyes red, the ace walking at their heel. They nod to you once. That's all. It's enough.

effects.text: Helped the rival find the ace that walked away, and gave them space to say sorry.
